newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats offer leader "honeymoon on probation".
newsitem.headline: HK democrats offer leader "honeymoon on probation".

text.p: The head of Hong Kong's biggest pro-democracy party offered the territory's Chinese leader-in-waiting a political honeymoon on Wednesday but also served notice the future chief executive was "on probation".

Tung Chee-hwa, a conservative patriot, won a historic vote by a 400-member China-controlled Selection Committee on Wednesday to become Hong Kong's first leader under Beijing rule when a century and a half of British colonial rule ends in 202 days.

"He (Tung) hasn't got the mandate of the Hong Kong people, and the Chinese government has made numerous statements recently which cause a lot of concerns," said Martin Lee, leader of the Democratic Party, the largest in Hong Kong's legislature.
"We want to help him as much as we can and we must give him the benefit of doubt," Lee told reporters.
He said Tung could expect qualified cooperation from the democrats amounting to a "honeymoon on probation".

"We sincerely hope that Mr Tung can now prove to Hong Kong people and the world that he is better than the unrepresentative system that produced him," Lee said. "What Hong Kong needs now is not a spokesman for China -- but an uncompromising defender of the Hong Kong's freedoms and way of life," he said.
Democrats fear civil liberties in the freewheeling capitalist city of 6.3 million may be curbed after the handover.
The Democratic Party, vocal critics of Chinese policies, has been branded as "subversive" and is conspicuously absent from China-appointed committees shaping future political structures.

Lee hoped Tung would safeguard the promised high degree of autonomy under a 1984 agreement between China and Britain on the return of Hong Kong and listen to the voice of Hong Kong people, including the voices of opposition, he said.
He said the Democrats would try to persuade the former shipping empire boss not to introduce laws restricting basic freedoms and not to reintroduce appointed seats on municipal and district councils.
The Democrats had sent a letter to the chief executive-designate requesting a meeting to discuss the concerns of Hong Kong people, Lee said.

The democratic camp spearheaded by Lee's Democratic Party won legislative elections held last year, but China has vowed to disband the legislature on handover day, install a new one of its own making, and roll back democratic reforms.
